security_audit.summary: All 143 static findings were adjudicated; most describe Markdown, local configuration, or expected service calls, with no evidence found of injection or deliberate exfiltration. Confirmed working proxy examples expose reusable authentication without transport encryption; the authenticated Chromium SOCKS5 example instead fails before connecting. Semantic findings identify token exposure through process arguments and command output, plus absent payment-budget checks in the automatic purchase example.

remediation.issue: Proxy credentials cross unencrypted SOCKS5 and HTTP proxy connections.
remediation.suggestion: Use authenticated TLS proxy transport or a secure tunnel before sending reusable tokens; destination HTTPS does not encrypt proxy authentication.

remediation.issue: Expanded tokens enter Python and curl process arguments despite environment-variable safety claims.
remediation.suggestion: Read secrets within Python from the environment, and pass curl request data and credentials through protected input channels instead of arguments.

remediation.issue: Rotation and recovery print newly issued tokens through the generic response formatter.
remediation.suggestion: Capture new tokens in protected local storage and redact them from standard output before showing results to an agent.

remediation.issue: The automatic payment example does not enforce the amount approved by the user.
remediation.suggestion: Validate challenge amount, asset, network, and recipient against the approved purchase before signing; reject changes and enforce a cumulative spending limit.

remediation.issue: The Chromium example configures unsupported SOCKS5 username and password authentication.
remediation.suggestion: Replace it with a supported browser proxy configuration protected by encrypted transport. Explain browser-specific authentication restrictions.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Purchase Example Omits Approved Spending Limit
semantic_findings.description: The TypeScript example configures automatic signing with a network restriction but no user-approved amount or budget policy. Following it provides no demonstrated check against an increased challenge amount, despite the main document requiring approval for a specific amount.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The shown configuration supplies no approved amount and performs no local quote comparison. Library defaults are not included, so their protections cannot be verified.

semantic_findings.title: Environment Tokens Still Leak Through Child Process Arguments
semantic_findings.description: The helper claims environment tokens avoid process listings, but expands them into Python arguments, curl request bodies, authorization headers, and proxy credentials. Local process inspection or command telemetry can expose reusable tokens even when callers avoid explicit token arguments.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Quoted shell expansion preserves argument boundaries but places the actual secret in child-process argv. Environment input does not prevent this explicit argument exposure.

semantic_findings.title: Rotation and Recovery Print Newly Issued Secret Tokens
semantic_findings.description: Rotation and recovery pipe complete responses through the generic formatter. Those documented responses contain replacement tokens, which can enter agent transcripts or logs. This contradicts the instruction to treat any token shown in output as compromised.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The formatter prints full JSON without redaction, and both helper commands send responses directly to it. Actual transcript exposure depends on execution context.

content.user_title: Manage Paid Proxy Access with x402socks
content.value_statement: Regional network tasks require available proxy exits, controlled spending, and reliable credentials. This skill provides discovery commands, x402 payment guidance, client examples, and token management.
actual_capabilities: Query service health, list available exit nodes, and summarize live package prices through the Bash helper.
Guide USDC purchases on Base using x402 challenges and a TypeScript payment-wrapper example.
Check token status and validity, request rotation, and submit signed credential recovery requests.
Test a selected proxy exit against a public IP-check service.
Provide curl, Python requests, and Node HTTP CONNECT configuration examples.
Explain payment failures, proxy authentication errors, DNS behavior, and plan session limits.
limitations: Purchases require a funded wallet, a signer, and explicit user approval; the Bash helper does not implement purchases.
Most helper commands require curl and Python 3; client examples need additional libraries. Chromium does not support the shown authenticated SOCKS5 configuration.
Service availability, package prices, regions, session limits, and data allowances depend on the live provider.
Examples lack encrypted proxy authentication and enforced payment limits; some helper commands expose tokens through arguments or output.

use_cases.title: Check Regional Application Access
use_cases.description: Inspect healthy exits and prepare an authorized regional request to an application you own.

use_cases.title: Plan Agent Network Spending
use_cases.description: Compare current package prices and session allowances before approving a bounded proxy purchase.

use_cases.title: Recover Paid Proxy Access
use_cases.description: Diagnose authentication failures and prepare wallet-signed recovery after a settled payment without purchasing the same access again.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Availability
prompt_templates.prompt: Check x402socks health and list healthy, enabled exits. Do not purchase access or access wallet credentials.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: inspect the service without spending money.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Packages
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare live packages for one agent needing [duration] and [data allowance]. Quote the lowest suitable price and wait for approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: select a package without authorizing payment.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Proxy Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose [error] using service health, node availability, and token validation. Keep secrets out of arguments and output. Do not rotate or purchase automatically.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: investigate an existing access problem.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Bounded Purchase
prompt_templates.prompt: Review a purchase for [package] capped at [amount] USDC on Base. Require exact challenge checks and protected token capture before signing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: identify safeguards required before a paid workflow.

output_examples.output: Access scope: public health, catalog, and node checks only. Eligible exits must be enabled and healthy. No purchase or wallet access authorized.

output_examples.input: A purchase settled, but no token was received.
output_examples.output: Recovery plan: retain the settlement transaction hash and verify the paying wallet. Prepare a fresh ownership signature; do not repeat the purchase.

output_examples.input: Review the purchase example before unattended use.
output_examples.output: Review result: the purchase example shows no approved spending limit. Proxy authentication needs encrypted transport. Helper tokens can reach process arguments and command output.

best_practices: Refresh catalog and node availability, then enforce the approved amount and payment parameters before signing.
Protect proxy authentication with encrypted transport, and keep tokens out of process arguments, command output, and transcripts.
Keep settlement references and use ownership-signed recovery instead of repeating a settled purchase.
anti_patterns: Treating a live payment challenge as permission to exceed the approved purchase amount.
Assuming environment substitution, destination HTTPS, or remote DNS prevents proxy-token exposure.
Using proxies to bypass explicit access prohibitions or purchasing replacement access before diagnosing an existing payment.

faq.question: Does the helper purchase proxy access?
faq.answer: No. It handles discovery, pricing, validation, rotation, recovery, and egress tests. Purchases use the documented payment-library workflow.

faq.question: Which payment network does the skill document?
faq.answer: It documents USDC on Base through x402. Inspect live challenge fields and enforce the user-approved amount before signing.

faq.question: Can I use the skill without spending money?
faq.answer: You can inspect public health, node availability, and catalog information without paying. Authenticated proxy access requires an existing token or purchase.

faq.question: Does an environment variable keep my token private?
faq.answer: Not by itself. The helper expands tokens into child-process arguments, and rotation or recovery can print replacement tokens.

faq.question: Does destination HTTPS protect proxy authentication?
faq.answer: No. Ordinary SOCKS5 and HTTP CONNECT authentication remain unencrypted on the client-to-proxy connection. Use protected proxy transport.

faq.question: What should I do after a settled purchase loses its token?
faq.answer: Use the settlement transaction hash and a fresh signature from the paying wallet for recovery. Do not purchase the same access again.
